provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Numbers to 100 review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count to 100.
The pupils should be able to fill missing numbers on a hundred chart.

Introduction:
We have learned to count to 100 before.
Today we will practice counting and finding missing numbers.

Content:
Count from 1 to 100 together.
Show a hundred chart with some numbers missing.
Point to the empty spaces and ask pupils to say the missing number.
Use Nigerian examples like counting naira notes or market items.

Class activity:
Give each pupil a hundred chart with gaps.
They work in pairs to fill in the missing numbers.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 100.
What number comes after 45?
What number is missing on your chart?

Summary:
We practiced counting to 100 and finding missing numbers.

topics.title: Number names review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write number names from one to twenty.
The pupils should be able to match numbers with their names.

Introduction:
We have learned number names before.
Today we will practice writing and matching them.

Content:
Say the number names from one to twenty.
Write the names on the board.
Show number cards and ask pupils to say the name.
Match numbers with their names using flashcards.

Class activity:
Give pupils number cards and word cards.
They work in groups to match numbers with correct names.

Evaluation questions:
Write the name for number 15.
Match 7 with its name.
What is the name for 20?

Summary:
We practiced writing and matching number names.

topics.title: Tens and ones
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify tens and ones in numbers.
The pupils should be able to bundle sticks to show tens and ones.

Introduction:
Numbers have tens and ones.
We will use sticks to show this.

Content:
Explain that 34 means 3 tens and 4 ones.
Show how to bundle ten sticks together to make a ten.
Use numbers like 25, 47, 63.
Count the bundles and loose sticks to find the number.

Class activity:
Give pupils bundles of ten sticks and loose sticks.
Call out a number and they make it with bundles and ones.

Evaluation questions:
How many tens in 46?
Show 28 with sticks.
What is 3 tens and 5 ones?

Summary:
We learned about tens and ones using sticks.

topics.title: Ordering numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to order numbers from biggest to smallest.
The pupils should be able to arrange number cards in order.

Introduction:
Numbers can be big or small.
Today we will put them in order.

Content:
Show numbers like 15, 8, 23, 12.
Explain biggest means largest number.
Smallest means least number.
Arrange them from biggest to smallest: 23, 15, 12, 8.

Class activity:
Give each group number cards.
They arrange the cards from biggest to smallest.

Evaluation questions:
Arrange 45, 23, 67, 12 from biggest to smallest.
What comes after 35?
What comes before 50?

Summary:
We learned to put numbers in order.

topics.title: Addition to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add numbers to make 10.
The pupils should be able to write addition sentences.

Introduction:
Adding means putting numbers together.
Today we find pairs that make 10.

Content:
Show pairs like 3 and 7 make 10.
4 and 6 make 10.
5 and 5 make 10.
Write addition sentences like 3 + 7 = 10.
Use fingers or objects to show adding.

Class activity:
Give pupils counters.
They find two groups that add to 10.

Evaluation questions:
What two numbers make 10?
Write 4 + 6 = ?
How many in 2 + 8?

Summary:
We practiced adding to make 10.

topics.title: Addition to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add numbers to 20 without carrying.
The pupils should be able to write addition sentences.

Introduction:
We can add bigger numbers now.
We will use sticks to help us.

Content:
Show how to add 12 + 5 using sticks.
Make 12 with one bundle and 2 sticks.
Add 5 more sticks.
Count all to get 17.
Do more examples like 14 + 3, 16 + 2.

Class activity:
Give pupils bundles and sticks.
They solve addition problems using the materials.

Evaluation questions:
Solve 13 + 4 = ?
Show 15 + 2 with sticks.
What is 11 + 6?

Summary:
We learned to add to 20 without carrying.

topics.title: Subtraction from 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to subtract numbers from 20.
The pupils should be able to write subtraction answers.

Introduction:
Subtraction means taking away.
We will use bundles to help us.

Content:
Show how to subtract 15-3 using sticks.
Make 15 with one bundle and 5 sticks.
Take away 3 sticks.
Count what is left to get 12.
Do more examples like 18-4, 20-5.

Class activity:
Give pupils bundles and sticks.
They solve subtraction problems using the materials.

Evaluation questions:
Solve 17-5 = ?
Show 16-2 with sticks.
What is 20-8?

Summary:
We learned to subtract from 20.

topics.title: Doubles and halves
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to find doubles of small numbers.
The pupils should be able to find halves of even numbers.

Introduction:
Double means two of the same.
Half means sharing into two equal parts.

Content:
Show doubles like double 6 is 12.
Double 7 is 14.
Show halves like half of 10 is 5.
Half of 8 is 4.
Use dominoes to show doubles.

Class activity:
Give pupils dominoes.
They find doubles and say the answer.

Evaluation questions:
What is double 5?
What is half of 12?
Show double 8 with fingers.

Summary:
We learned about doubles and halves.

topics.title: Shapes review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify circle, square, triangle, rectangle.
The pupils should be able to sort shapes into groups.

Introduction:
Shapes are all around us.
We will learn about different shapes.

Content:
Show and name circle, square, triangle, rectangle.
Circle is round like a plate.
Square has four equal sides.
Triangle has three sides.
Rectangle has four long sides.

Class activity:
Give pupils a shape sorting tray.
They sort objects by shape.

Evaluation questions:
Name this shape (show circle).
How many sides does a triangle have?
Sort these shapes into groups.

Summary:
We learned about different shapes.

topics.title: Revision and number quiz
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer mixed number questions.
The pupils should be able to participate in number games.

Introduction:
We have learned many number things.
Today we play games to remember.

Content:\Review counting to 100.
Review addition and subtraction.
Review shapes.
Play number games with the whole class.

Class activity:
Number quiz with teams.
Answer questions to win points.

Evaluation questions:
Count to 100.
Solve 8 + 7.
What shape has three sides?

Summary:
We played games to remember what we learned.
